associations.rationale: The formal type directly states or defines the item: Produces a finite algebraic candidate satisfying the displayed conditions, with a rank bound and uniqueness up to algebra equivalence among the specified candidates.
The formal type directly states or defines the item: Guarantees a finite algebraic candidate meeting the two displayed conditions.
The formal type directly states or defines the item: Guarantees a finite algebraic candidate meeting the three displayed conditions.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: Shows that two candidates satisfying the stated pair of shared conditions are algebra equivalent.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: Shows that two candidates satisfying the other stated pair of shared conditions are algebra equivalent.
The formal type directly states or defines the item: Bounds the rank of a candidate by that of the ambient algebra under the stated conditions.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: Bounds the rank of a candidate by that of the ambient algebra under the other stated conditions.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: The relation holds when both arguments are the same ring.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: Reverses an instance of the relation between two rings.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: Composes two compatible instances of the relation between rings.
The formal type provides an exact-module supporting component: The displayed relation holds for a field paired with itself.
